text: A spherical body of radius $r$ and density $σ$ falls freely through a viscous liquid having density $ρ$ and viscosity $η$ and attains a terminal velocity $v_{0}$. Estimated maximum error in the quantity $η$ is : (Ignore errors associated with $σ$, $ρ$ and $g$, gravitational acceleration)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a spherical body falls through a viscous liquid, the forces acting on it are,

Weight ( W ) which is acting downwards.

Up thrust ( $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{b}}$ ) is acting upwards (due to buoyancy).

Viscous Drag $(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}})$ is acting upwards (opposing the motion).


[IMG]


The radius of the spherical body is $r$.

The density of the body is $σ$

So, the weight of the spherical body is,

$\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{mg}=(σ\mathrm{V})\mathrm{g}=σ\left [\frac{4}{3}π\mathrm{r}^{3}\right ]\mathrm{g}$

The density of the liquid is $ρ$, and when body is completely inside the liquid, the up thrust is,

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}=ρ\mathrm{Vg}=\frac{4}{3}π\mathrm{r}^{3}ρ\mathrm{g}$

The viscous drag acting on the body is

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}=6πη\mathrm{rv}$

Terminal velocity is reached when the net force on the body becomes zero (acceleration is zero).

$\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}σg=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}ρg+6πηrv_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $6πηrv_{0}=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}g(σ-ρ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $η=\frac{\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}g(σ-ρ)}{6πrv_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $η=\frac{2r^{2}g(σ-ρ)}{9v_{0}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $η=\frac{\left [\frac{2g(σ-ρ)}{9}\right ]r^{2}}{v_{0}}$

As it is given to ignore errors associated with $σ,ρ$, and g . Therefore, $\left [\frac{2\mathrm{g}(σ-ρ)}{9}\right ]$ is a constant $(\mathrm{k})$.

$η=\mathrm{k}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{r}^{2}}{\mathrm{v}_{0}}$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides:

$\ln (η)=\ln (\mathrm{k})+2\ln (\mathrm{r})-\ln (\mathrm{v}_{0})$

On differentiating both sides:

$\frac{dη}{η}=0+\frac{2dr}{r}-\frac{dv_{0}}{v_{0}}$

For maximum error, we sum the absolute values of the individual errors because errors always propagate in a way that maximizes the uncertainty:

$\frac{\Delta η}{η}=\frac{2\Delta r}{r}+\frac{\Delta v_{0}}{v_{0}}\text{or}\frac{\Delta η}{η}=-\frac{2\Delta r}{r}-\frac{\Delta v_{0}}{v_{0}}$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

text: Keeping the significant figures in view, the sum of the physical quantities 52.01 m, 153.2 m and 0.123 m is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In addition, or subtraction, the final result should be reported to the same number of decimal places as the measurement with the least number of decimal places. This ensures the result is no more precise than the least precise measurement.

The given measured values are,

$52.01\mathrm{m}:2$ decimal places.

153.2 m : 1 decimal place.

0.123 m : 3 decimal places.

The measurement with the least number of decimal places is 153.2 m ( 1 decimal place). Therefore, our final answer must be rounded to one decimal place.

$52.01+153.2+0.123=205.333\mathrm{m}$

Now, we round 205.333 to one decimal place :

The digit at the first decimal place is $3\to 205.33$

The digit following it is 3 (which is less than 5 ) → 205.3

Therefore, the rounded result is 205.3 m . Hence, the correct option is (A)

A large drum having radius $R$ is spinning around its axis with angular velocity $ω$, as shown in figure.
 The minimum value of $ω$ so that a body of mass $M$ remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass $M$ as $μ$, is :
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When the drum rotates, the mass M experiences forces :

1. Weight $(\mathrm{Mg})$ acts vertically downwards.

2. Normal reaction ( N ) acts horizontally toward the centre of the drum. This provides the necessary centripetal force.

3. Frictional force (f) acts vertically upwards, opposing the tendency of the mass to slide down due to gravity.


[IMG]


For the body to remain at rest with respect to the cylindrical surface, the vertical forces must be balanced :

$\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{Mg}$

The horizontal normal force provides the centripetal acceleration ( $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{c}}=\mathrm{R}ω^{2}$ ) :

$N=MRω^{2}$

The frictional force (f) is a self-adjusting force up to a maximum limit (limiting friction). For the body to stay at rest relative to the wall :

$\mathrm{f}\leq \mathrm{f}_{\max }$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{f}\leq μ\mathrm{N}$

Substituting the values of f and N into this inequality :

$Mg\leq μ\left (MRω^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $g\leq μRω^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω^{2}\geq \frac{g}{μR}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω\geq \sqrt{\frac{g}{μR}}$

Therefore, the minimum angular speed is $ω_{\min }=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{g}}{μ\mathrm{R}}}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Two known resistances of $R\Omega$ and $2R\Omega$ and one unknown resistance $X\Omega$ are connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. If the equivalent resistance between points $A$ and $B$ in the circuit is $X\Omega$, then the value of $X$ is $__________$ $\Omega$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Resistors 2R and $X$ are connected in series.

$\mathrm{R}_{1}=2\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{X}$

And the combination of $(2R+X)$ is connected across $R$ in parallel.

$\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_{1}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{1}{2\mathrm{R}+\mathrm{X}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{X}=\frac{R+(2R+X)}{R(2R+X)}$

$\Rightarrow$ $X(3R+X)=R(2R+X)$

$\Rightarrow$ $3RX+X^{2}=2R^{2}+RX$

$\Rightarrow$ $X^{2}+2RX-2R^{2}=0$

Using the quadratic equation formula,

$X=\frac{-2R\pm \sqrt{(2R)^{2}-4(1)(-2R^{2})}}{2\times 1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $X=\frac{-2R\pm \sqrt{4R^{2}+8R^{2}}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $X=\frac{-2R\pm \sqrt{12R^{2}}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $X=\frac{-2R\pm 2\sqrt{3}R}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $X=-R\pm \sqrt{3}R$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{X}=(-1\pm \sqrt{3})\mathrm{R}$

Since resistance cannot be negative, we take the positive root:

$\mathrm{X}=(\sqrt{3}-1)\mathrm{R}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: The r.m.s. speed of oxygen molecules at 47 °C is equal to that of the hydrogen molecules kept at $_________$ °C. (Mass of oxygen molecule/mass of hydrogen molecule = 32/2)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to the Kinetic Theory of Gases, the r.m.s speed of an ideal gas is given by :

$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3\mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}$

Where T is the absolute temperature and M is the molecular mass (in kg ).

It is given that the r.m.s. speed of oxygen $(\mathrm{O}_{2})$ at $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}$ is equal to the r.m.s. speed of hydrogen $(\mathrm{H}_{2})$ at $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}$.

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}(\mathrm{O}_{2})}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}(\mathrm{H}_{2})}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{\frac{3\mathrm{RT}_{\mathrm{O}2}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{3\mathrm{RT}_{\mathrm{H}2}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{H}2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{O}2}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}2}}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}2}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{H}2}}$

Temperature of oxygen is $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}=47+273=320\mathrm{K}$.

Molar masses are $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}=32\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=2\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg}$.

$\frac{320}{32}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}2}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $10=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}2}}{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=20\mathrm{K}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=20-273$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=-253^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$

Therefore, the rms speed of oxygen molecules at $47^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ is equal to that of the hydrogen molecules kept at $-253^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm in the arrangement as shown in the figure. If P is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length AP is $________ cm$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When the galvanometer (G) shows a zero reading, it means no current is flowing through the galvanometer branch. This occurs when the circuit is in a balanced state.


[IMG]


Resistance $\mathrm{R}_{1}=6\Omega$.

Resistance $\mathrm{R}_{2}=4\Omega$.

Let the length AP be l . Its resistance is $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{AP}}$.

Since the total length AB is 50 cm , the length of PB is ( $50-\mathrm{l}$ ). Its resistance is $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{PB}}$.

The resistance R of a uniform wire is given by the formula :

$\mathrm{R}=\frac{ρ\mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{A}}$

Where $ρ$ is resistivity, L is length, and A is the cross-sectional area. Since the wire is uniform, the resistance is directly proportional to the length ( $\mathrm{R}\propto \mathrm{L}$ ).

$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{AP}}=\mathrm{k}\cdot \mathrm{l}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{PB}}=\mathrm{k}\cdot (50-\mathrm{l})$

where $\mathrm{k}=\frac{ρ}{\mathrm{A}}$ is a constant.

For a balanced bridge:

$\frac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{AP}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{PB}}}$

Substituting the known values :

$\frac{6}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{k}\cdot \mathrm{l}}{\mathrm{k}\cdot (50-\mathrm{l})}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{3}{2}=\frac{l}{50-l}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3(50-l)=2l$

$\Rightarrow$ $150-3l=2l$

$\Rightarrow$ $150=5l$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{l}=\frac{150}{5}=30\mathrm{cm}$

Therefore, the length of AP is 30 cm . Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$, are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ where $r_{1}>r_{2}$. The measured liquid heights in these tubes are $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid above the lowest point of miniscus]. The heights $h_{1}$ and $h_{2}$ and surface tensions $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ satisfy the relation :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a capillary tube is dipped in a liquid, the liquid rises due to surface tension until the upward force of surface tension is balanced by the weight of the liquid column.

The surface tension T acts along the circumference of the meniscus. If $θ$ is the contact angle, the vertical component of the force is :

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{up}}=\mathrm{T}\cos θ\times (2π\mathrm{r})$

The weight of the liquid column of height h is :

$W=\left (πr^{2}h\right )ρg$

At equilibrium :

$\mathrm{T}\cos θ(2π\mathrm{r})=π\mathrm{r}^{2}\mathrm{h}ρ\mathrm{g}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{h}=\frac{2\mathrm{T}\cos θ}{\mathrm{r}ρ\mathrm{g}}$

If we assume the two liquids refers to the same substance, then:

$\mathrm{T}_{1}=\mathrm{T}_{2}\ldots$ (i) (Surface tension is a property of the material and temperature).

$ρ$ and $g$ are constant.

$θ$ is constant.

This results the relationship: $\mathrm{h}\propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{r}}$.

We are given that $r_{1}>r_{2}\Rightarrow \frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}>1$.

So, the ratio of heights of capillary rise,

$\frac{\mathrm{h}_{1}}{\mathrm{h}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{2}}<1\Rightarrow \mathrm{h}_{1}<\mathrm{h}_{2}\ldots (ii)$

From both the relations, $\mathrm{h}_{1}<\mathrm{h}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{T}_{1}=\mathrm{T}_{2}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
A particle having electric charge $3\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$ and mass $6\times 10^{-27}\mathrm{kg}$ is accelerated by applying an electric potential of 1.21 V . 

Wavelength of the matter wave associated with the particle is $α\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{m}$. The value of $α$ is $____$ . 

(Take Planck's constant $=6.6\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}.\mathrm{s}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a particle of charge $q$ is accelerated through a potential difference $V$, the work done on the particle is converted into its kinetic energy (K):

$\mathrm{K}=\mathrm{qV}$

Given:

Charge $\mathrm{q}=3\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}$

Potential $\mathrm{V}=1.21\mathrm{V}$

$K=\left (3\times 10^{-19}\right )\times (1.21)=3.63\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{J}$

The momentum ( p ) of a particle of mass m is related to its kinetic energy ( K ) by:

$K=\frac{p^{2}}{2m}\Rightarrow p=\sqrt{2mK}$

Substituting $\mathrm{K}=\mathrm{qV}$ :

$\mathrm{p}=\sqrt{2\mathrm{mqV}}$

The de-Broglie wavelength is given by:

$λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}}$

Substituting the expression for momentum:

$λ=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2\mathrm{mqV}}}$

Substituting the given values:

$\mathrm{h}=6.6\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}.\mathrm{s},\mathrm{m}=6\times 10^{-27}\mathrm{kg},\mathrm{q}=3\times 10^{-19}\mathrm{C}\text{and}\mathrm{V}=1.21\mathrm{V}$

So, the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the particle is,

$λ=\frac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2\times \left (6\times 10^{-27}\right )\times \left (3\times 10^{-19}\right )\times 1.21}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{36\times 10^{-46}\times 1.21}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{6\times 10^{-23}\times 1.1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{6.6\times 10^{-34}}{6.6\times 10^{-23}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=1\times 10^{-11}\mathrm{m}=α\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{m}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=10\times 10^{-12}=α\times 10^{-12}\Rightarrow α=10$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 10 . 

Hence, the correct answer is $𝟏 𝟎$.

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase as the screen is moved away from the plane of the slits
Statement II : In a Young's double slit experiment, the angular separation of fringes will increase when monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of higher wavelength
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In YDSE, the linear position of the $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe on the screen is given by :

$\mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{d}}$

Where :

$λ=$ wavelength of light used.

$\mathrm{D}=$ distance between the slits and the screen.

$\mathrm{d}=$ distance between the two slits.


[IMG]


The linear fringe width $(β)$, which is the distance between two consecutive bright or dark fringes, is :

$β=y_{n+1}-y_{n}=\frac{λD}{d}$

The angular separation (or angular fringe width) $θ_{β}$ is the angle subtended by the fringe width at the slits. For small angles :

$θ_{β}\approx \frac{β}{D}$

Substituting the value of $β$ :

$θ_{β}=\frac{\left (\frac{λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{d}}\right )}{\mathrm{D}}=\frac{λ}{\mathrm{d}}$

Statement I says that angular separation $(θ_{β})$ increases as the screen is moved away (D increases).

From the formula $θ_{β}=λ/d$, we can see that $θ_{β}$ depends only on the wavelength ( $λ$ ) and the slit separation (d).

$θ_{β}\propto λ\ldots \text{(i),}θ_{β}\propto \frac{1}{d}\ldots \text{(ii)}$

It is independent of the distance to the screen (D).

Therefore, Statement I is false.

Statement II says that $θ$ increases when a source of higher wavelength is used.

From the formula $θ_{β}\propto λ$, i.e., if $λ$ increases, $θ$ must also increase.

Therefore, Statement II is true.

Therefore, Statement I is false and Statement II is true. 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: The kinetic energy of a simple harmonic oscillator is oscillating with angular frequency of 176 rad/s. The frequency of this simple harmonic oscillator is $______ Hz$. [ take $π=\frac{22}{7}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For displacement $x=A\sin ωt$, the kinetic energy is

$K=\dfrac{1}{2}mω^{2}A^{2}\cos ^{2}ωt=\dfrac{1}{4}mω^{2}A^{2}(1+\cos 2ωt)$

so the kinetic energy oscillates with angular frequency $2ω$.

$2ω=176\text{rad s}^{-1}\Rightarrow ω=88\text{rad s}^{-1}$

$f=\dfrac{ω}{2π}=\dfrac{88}{2\times \frac{22}{7}}=\dfrac{88\times 7}{44}=14\text{Hz}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Two cars A and B each of mass $10^{3}$ kg are moving on parallel tracks separated by a distance of 10 m, in same direction with speeds 72 km/h and 36 km/h. The magnitude of angular momentum of car A with respect to car B is $________ J$·s.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Speed of car $A,v_{A}=72\times \frac{5}{18}=20\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Speed of car B, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{B}}=36\times \frac{5}{18}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Since both cars are moving in the same direction, the relative velocity of car $A$ with respect to $\mathrm{car}B\left (⃗{v}_{AB}\right )$ is :

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{A}}-\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{B}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{AB}}=20-10=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$


[IMG]


Angular momentum of a point mass relative to an observer is defined as:

$\vec{\mathrm{L}}=\vec{\mathrm{r}}\times \vec{\mathrm{p}}$

Where $\vec{\mathrm{r}}$ is the position vector and $\vec{\mathrm{p}}$ is the linear momentum ( $\mathrm{m}\vec{\mathrm{v}}$ ).

The perpendicular distance $(\mathrm{r}_{⟂}=\mathrm{d})$ between the two parallel tracks:

$\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{m}\cdot \mathrm{v}_{\text{relative}}\cdot \mathrm{r}_{⟂}$

Given values are,

Mass $\mathrm{m}=10^{3}\mathrm{kg}$

Relative speed $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{AB}}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Perpendicular distance $\mathrm{r}_{⟂}=10\mathrm{m}$

Substituting the values into the formula :

$L=\left (10^{3}\right )\times (10)\times (10)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{L}=10^{5}\mathrm{J}.\mathrm{s}$

Therefore, the angular momentum of the car A with respect to B is $10^{5}\mathrm{J}$. s.

text:
An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, $σ=10\mathrm{mho}/\mathrm{m}$. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is $____$.

$\left [\text{Take}\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}\mathrm{Nm}^{2}/\mathrm{C}^{2}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Ohm's Law in point form, the conduction current density is proportional to the electric field (E) :

$\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{c}}=σ\mathrm{E}$

The maximum value occurs when the electric field is at its peak $(\mathrm{E}_{0})$ :

$(\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{c}})_{\max }=σ\mathrm{E}_{0}$

Displacement current density arises from a time-varying electric field. For an electromagnetic wave, the electric field can be represented as $E=E_{0}\sin (ωt)$.

Maxwell defined displacement current density as :

$\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{d}}=𝜖\frac{𝜕\mathrm{E}}{𝜕\mathrm{t}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{d}}=𝜖\frac{𝜕}{𝜕\mathrm{t}}(\mathrm{E}_{0}\sin (ω\mathrm{t}))=𝜖ω\mathrm{E}_{0}\cos (ω\mathrm{t})$

The maximum value occurs when the cosine term is 1 :

$(\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{d}})_{\max }=𝜖ω\mathrm{E}_{0}$

The ratio of the maximum values is:

Ratio $=\frac{(\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{c}})_{\text{\max }}}{(\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{d}})_{\text{\max }}}=\frac{σ\mathrm{E}_{0}}{𝜖ω\mathrm{E}_{0}}=\frac{σ}{𝜖ω}$

The conductivity $(σ)$ of the medium is, $σ=10\mathrm{mho}/\mathrm{m}$

The angular frequency $(ω)$ is $2π\mathrm{f}=2π\times \left (100\times 10^{6}\right )=2π\times 10^{8}\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$

Since no specific medium permittivity is given, we use the permittivity of free space ( $𝜖_{0}$ ).

Given $\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}$, then $𝜖_{0}=\frac{1}{36π\times 10^{9}}$.

Substituting these values into the ratio:

Ratio $=\frac{10}{\frac{1}{36π\times 10 9}\times 2π\times 10^{8}}=\frac{10\times 36π\times 10^{9}}{2π\times 10^{8}}$

Ratio $=180\times 10^{1}=1800$

Therefore, the ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is 1800 . 

Hence, the correct answer is $𝟏 𝟖 𝟎 𝟎$.

text:
The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius 6 mm in a viscous fluid is $20\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius 3 mm in the same fluid will be
$____$ $\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a spherical ball falls through a viscous fluid, it eventually reaches a constant speed called terminal velocity. This occurs when the net force acting on the ball is zero.


[IMG]


The forces acting on the ball are :

Weight (W) which acts downwards. $\mathrm{W}=\frac{4}{3}π\mathrm{r}^{3}σ\mathrm{g}$ (where $σ$ is the density of the ball).

Up-thrust $(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}})$ is Acting upwards. $F_{B}=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}ρg$ (where $ρ$ is the density of the fluid).

Viscous drag $(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}})$ is acting upwards. According to Stokes' Law, $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}=6πη\mathrm{r}\mathrm{v}$, where $η$ is the viscosity of fluid and v is the speed of the ball.

At equilibrium :

$\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}σg=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}ρg+6πηrv$

$\Rightarrow$ $6πηrv=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}g(σ-ρ)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}=\frac{2\mathrm{r}^{2}\mathrm{g}(σ-ρ)}{9η}$

For balls of the same material in the same fluid :

$\mathrm{v}\propto \mathrm{r}^{2}$

Therefore :

$\frac{\mathrm{v}_{2}}{\mathrm{v}_{1}}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{r}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}_{1}}\right )^{2}$

Initial radius of the ball is $r_{1}=6\mathrm{mm}$ and the initial terminal velocity is $v_{1}=20\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$

Final radius of the ball is $r_{2}=3\mathrm{mm}$

Substituting the values :

text:
An infinitely long straight wire carrying current $I$ is bent in a planar shape as shown in the diagram. The radius of the circular part is $r$. The magnetic field at the centre $O$ of the circular loop is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The segments AB and DE together form an infinitely long straight wire.

For an infinite wire the magnitude of the magnetic field at distance r is given as

$\mathrm{B}_{\text{straight}}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2π\mathrm{r}}$

Using the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, if the thumb points in the direction of current I (along +y ), the fingers curl out of the page at point O , i.e., in the +x direction.

$\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\text{straight}}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2π\mathrm{r}}\hat{ı}$

The circular part is a nearly complete loop of radius r .

For a circular loop at its centre the magnitude of the magnetic field is given as,

$\mathrm{B}_{\text{loop}}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2\mathrm{r}}$

Using the Right-Hand Rule for loops, curling the fingers in the direction of the current (clockwise in the yz -plane) the thumb points into the page, which is the -x direction.

$\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{loop}}=-\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2\mathrm{r}}\hat{\mathrm{i}}$

The total field is the vector sum of both parts :

$\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\text{total}}=\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\text{straight}}+\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{loop}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{total}}=\left (\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2π\mathrm{r}}\right )\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\left (-\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2\mathrm{r}}\right )\hat{\mathrm{i}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{\mathrm{B}}_{\text{total}}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2\mathrm{r}}\left [\frac{1}{π}-1\right ]\hat{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2π\mathrm{r}}[1-π]\hat{\mathrm{i}}=-\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2π\mathrm{r}}[π-1]\hat{\mathrm{i}}$

So, the magnetic field at the centre O of the circular loop is $=-\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{2π\mathrm{r}}[π-1]\hat{\mathrm{i}}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A diatomic gas $(γ=1.4)$ does 100 J of work when it is expanded isobarically. Then the heat given to the gas $____$ J.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An isobaric process occurs at constant pressure (P). For isobaric process :

The work done is $\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{P}\Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{nR}\Delta \mathrm{T}$

The change in internal energy is $\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{n}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}\Delta \mathrm{T}$

Heat added to the system is, $\mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{n}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}\Delta \mathrm{T}$

The ratio of specific heats is defined as $γ=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}}$.

Also, from Mayer's relation $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}-\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}$.

The ratio of Heat to Work is:

$\frac{Q}{W}=\frac{nC_{p}\Delta T}{nR\Delta T}=\frac{C_{p}}{R}$

Substituting $\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}}-\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}}$ :

$\frac{Q}{W}=\frac{C_{p}}{C_{p}-C_{v}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{W}}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{C}\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{C}\mathrm{v}}}{\left (\frac{\mathrm{C}\mathrm{p}}{\mathrm{C}\mathrm{v}}\right )-1}=\frac{γ}{γ-1}$

The work done is given as, $\mathrm{W}=100\mathrm{J}$ and the ratio of specific heats $γ=1.4$ (for a diatomic gas) So,

$\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{100}=\frac{1.4}{1.4-1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{Q}{100}=\frac{1.4}{0.4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{Q}{100}=3.5$

$\Rightarrow$ $Q=350\mathrm{J}$

Therefore, the heat given to the gas is 350 J . 

Hence, the correct option is $𝟑 𝟓 𝟎$.

text:
The energy of an electron in an orbit of the Bohr's atom is $-0.04E_{0}$ eV where $E_{0}$ is the ground state energy. If $L$ is the angular momentum of the electron in this orbit and $h$ is the Planck's constant, then

$\frac{2πL}{h}$ is $________$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the Bohr model of the atom, the energy of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit $(E_{n})$ is related to the ground state energy ( $\mathrm{E}_{0}$ ) by the formula :

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{n}}=-\frac{\mathrm{E}_{0}}{\mathrm{n}^{2}}$

It is given that the energy in the current orbit is $-0.04\mathrm{E}_{0}\mathrm{eV}$.

$-0.04\mathrm{E}_{0}=-\frac{\mathrm{E}_{0}}{\mathrm{n}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $0.04=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}^{2}=\frac{100}{4}=25$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}=\sqrt{25}=5$

So, the electron is in the $5^{\text{th}}$ orbit of the Bohr's atom.

Bohr's second postulate states that the angular momentum of an electron is quantized and is an integral multiple of $\mathrm{h}/2π$ :

$\mathrm{L}=\frac{\mathrm{nh}}{2π}$

Where n is the principal quantum number (orbit number).

$\frac{2πL}{h}=n=5$

Therefore, the value of $\frac{2πL}{h}$ is 5 . 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
In a Young's double slit experiment set up, the two slits are kept 0.4 mm apart and screen is placed at 1 m from slits. If a thin transparent sheet of thickness $20μ\mathrm{m}$ is introduced in front of one of the slits then center bright fringe shifts by 20 mm on the screen. 

The refractive index of transparent sheet is given by $\frac{α}{10}$, where $α$ is $____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


When a transparent sheet of thickness t and refractive index $μ$ is placed in front of one slit, the optical path length of the light from that slit increases.

Extra path length introduced is $\Delta \mathrm{x}=(μ-1)\mathrm{t}\ldots$ (i)

In YDSE, the path length at a point is given as $\Delta \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{d}\sin θ\Rightarrow \sin θ=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{d}}\ldots$ (ii)

For small angle, $\sin θ\approx \tan θ\approx θ$ (in radians).

Also, $\tan θ=\frac{\Delta y}{D}\ldots$ (iii)

From (i), (ii) and (iii);

$\frac{\Delta y}{D}=\frac{\Delta x}{d}$

$\Rightarrow \Delta y=\frac{D\Delta x}{d}=\frac{D(μ-1)t}{d}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta y=\frac{D(μ-1)t}{d}\Rightarrow (μ-1)=\frac{\Delta y\cdot d}{D\cdot t}$

$\Rightarrow μ=\frac{\Delta y\cdot d}{D\cdot t}+1$

Where :

$\mathrm{D}=$ distance between the slits and the screen $=1\mathrm{m}$.

$\mathrm{d}=$ distance between the two slits $=0.4\mathrm{mm}=0.4\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$.

Sheet thickness is $\mathrm{t}=20μ\mathrm{m}=20\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}$

Fringe shift is $\Delta y=20\mathrm{mm}=20\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$

Substituting these values,

$μ=\frac{\left (20\times 10^{-3}\right )\times \left (0.4\times 10^{-3}\right )}{1\times \left (20\times 10^{-6}\right )}+1$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ=\frac{8\times 10^{-6}}{20\times 10^{-6}}+1$

$\Rightarrow$ $μ=0.4+1=1.4=\frac{14}{10}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{14}{10}=\frac{α}{10}\Rightarrow α=14$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 14 .

As shown in the diagram, when the incident ray is parallel to base of the prism, the emergent ray grazes along the second surface.

If refractive index of the material of prism is $\sqrt{2}$, the angle $θ$ of prism is.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The incident ray is parallel to the base where the base angle is $45^{\circ }$.


[IMG]


If the ray is parallel to the base, the angle of incidence i with the normal to the first surface is also $45^{\circ }$

Let the refractive index of the prism be $μ=\sqrt{2}$ and air be $μ_{\text{air}}=1$.

Applying Snell's Law at the first surface :

$μ_{\mathrm{air}}\sin (\mathrm{i})=μ\sin (\mathrm{r}_{1})$

$\Rightarrow$ $1\times \sin (45^{\circ })=\sqrt{2}\times \sin (\mathrm{r}_{1})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}\sin (\mathrm{r}_{1})$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin (r_{1})=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $r_{1}=30^{\circ }$

It is given that the emergent ray grazes along the second surface. This means the angle of emergence e is $90^{\circ }$.

This occurs when the angle of incidence inside the prism at the second surface $(\mathrm{r}_{2})$ is equal to the critical angle (C).

Applying Snell's Law at the second surface :

$μ\sin (\mathrm{r}_{2})=μ_{\mathrm{air}}\sin (90^{\circ })$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{2}\times \sin (\mathrm{r}_{2})=1\times 1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin (r_{2})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{r}_{2}=45^{\circ }$

For any prism, the relationship between the apex angle A and the internal refracted angles is :

$\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{r}_{1}+\mathrm{r}_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{A}=30^{\circ }+45^{\circ }=75^{\circ }$

Sum of angles in a triangle is $180^{\circ }$ :

$45^{\circ }+θ+\mathrm{A}=180^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $45^{\circ }+θ+75^{\circ }=180^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $120^{\circ }+θ=180^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow$ $θ=60^{\circ }$

So, the angle $θ$ of prism is $60^{\circ }$. 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A body of mass 2 kg is moving along x-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by $x(t)=αt^{2}+βt+γ$ m, where $α=1m/s^{2}$, $β=1m/s$ and $γ=1m$. The work done on the body during the time interval $t=2s$ to $t=3s$, is $________ J$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Velocity ( $v$ ) is the rate of change of displacement ( $x$ ) with respect to time ( $t$ ) :

$v(t)=\frac{dx}{dt}$

The displacement function is given as:

$x(t)=αt^{2}+βt+γ$

Differentiating with respect to $t$ :

$v(t)=\frac{d}{dt}\left (αt^{2}+βt+γ\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $v(t)=2αt+β$

Substituting the given values $\left (α=1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2},β=1\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}\right )$ :

$v(t)=2(1)t+1$

$\Rightarrow$ $v(t)=2t+1$

Initial velocity $(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}})$ at $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ :

$\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}=2(2)+1=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Final velocity $(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{f}})$ at $\mathrm{t}=3\mathrm{s}$ :

$v_{f}=2(3)+1=7\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Using Work-Energy Theorem formula,

$\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{K}\cdot \mathrm{E}\cdot =\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}\left (\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{f}}^{2}-\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{i}}^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times \left (7^{2}-5^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=1\times (49-25)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=24\mathrm{J}$

Therefore, the work done on the body during the given time interval is 24 J . 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A battery with EMF $E$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected across a resistance $R$. The power consumption in $R$ will be maximum when:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


The total resistance of the circuit is $(R+r)$.

Using Ohm's Law, the current I flowing through the circuit is:

$I=\frac{E}{R+r}$

The power consumption P in the external resistor R is given by the formula:

$\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{I}^{2}\mathrm{R}$

Substituting the expression for I:

$P=\left (\frac{E}{R+r}\right )^{2}R=\frac{E^{2}R}{(R+r)^{2}}$

To find the value of R for which P is maximum, we differentiate P with respect to R and set the derivative to zero ( $\frac{\mathrm{dP}}{\mathrm{dR}}=0$ ).

$\frac{dP}{dR}=E^{2}\left [\frac{(R+r)^{2}1-R\cdot 2(R+r)}{(R+r)^{4}}\right ]=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(R+r)^{2}-2R(R+r)=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(R+r)-2R=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $r-R=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{r}$

Therefore, the power consumption in the external load R is at its maximum when the external resistance is equal to the internal resistance of the battery, $\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{R}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Consider two identical metallic spheres of radius $R$ each having charge $Q$ and mass $m$. Their centers have an initial separation of $4R$. Both the spheres are given an initial speed of $u$ towards each other. The minimum value of $u$, so that they can just touch each other is:
(Take $k=\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}$ and assume $kQ^{2}>Gm^{2}$ where $G$ is the Gravitational constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


At the start, the spheres are moving towards each other.

Since there are two spheres of mass $m$ moving with speed $u$, so the initial kinetic energy is,

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mu}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mu}^{2}=\mathrm{mu}^{2}$

Initial electrostatic potential energy is,

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ei}}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}$

Initial gravitational potential energy is :

$U_{gi}=-\frac{G\mathrm{m}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}$

When the spheres just touch, their centres are separated by a distance equal to the sum of their radii $(R+R=2R)$. To find the minimum $u$, we assume they come to a momentary rest at this point.

Total final kinetic energy, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}=0$

Final electrostatic potential energy is,

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ef}}=\frac{\mathrm{k}\mathrm{Q}^{2}}{2\mathrm{R}}$

Final gravitational potential energy is :

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{gf}}=-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{2\mathrm{R}}$

The total energy remains constant :

$K_{i}+U_{ei}+U_{gi}=K_{f}+U_{ef}+U_{gf}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{mu}^{2}+\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}=0+\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{2\mathrm{R}}-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{2\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{mu}^{2}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{2\mathrm{R}}-\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}\right )-\left (\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{2\mathrm{R}}-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{mu}^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{mu}^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{4\mathrm{R}}\left (1-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{u}^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}{4\mathrm{mR}}\left (1-\frac{\mathrm{Gm}^{2}}{\mathrm{kQ}^{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $u=\sqrt{\frac{kQ^{2}}{4mR}\left (1-\frac{Gm^{2}}{kQ^{2}}\right )}$

text: A capacitor C is first charged fully with potential difference of $V_{0}$ and disconnected from the battery. The charged capacitor is connected across an inductor having inductance L. In $t$ s, 25% of the initial energy in the capacitor is transferred to the inductor. The value of $t$ is $________ s$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a charged capacitor is connected to an inductor, the energy oscillates between the electric field of the capacitor and the magnetic field of the inductor.

The charge q on the capacitor at any time t is given by :

$\mathrm{q}(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{Q}_{0}\cos (ω\mathrm{t})$

Where :

$\mathrm{Q}_{0}$ is the initial maximum charge.

$ω$ is the angular frequency, defined as $ω=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{LC}}}$.

Initially all energy is in the capacitor.


[IMG]


$\mathrm{U}_{0}=\frac{\mathrm{Q}_{0}^{2}}{2\mathrm{C}}$

Energy in capacitor at time t is :

$U_{C}(t)=\frac{q(t)^{2}}{2C}=\frac{(Q_{0}\cos (ωt))^{2}}{2C}=U_{0}\cos ^{2}(ωt)$

By conservation of energy the energy stored in inductor as magnetic field,

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{L}}=\mathrm{U}_{0}-\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{C}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{L}}(\mathrm{t})=\mathrm{U}_{0}\left (1-\cos ^{2}(ω\mathrm{t})\right )=\mathrm{U}_{0}\sin ^{2}(ω\mathrm{t})$

It is that $25%$ of the initial energy is transferred to the inductor :

$\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{U}_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $U_{0}\sin ^{2}(ωt)=\frac{1}{4}U_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\sin ^{2}(ω\mathrm{t})=\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow\sin (ω\mathrm{t})=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrowω\mathrm{t}=\frac{π}{6}$

$\Rightarrow\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{LC}}}=\frac{π}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{t}=\frac{π\sqrt{\mathrm{LC}}}{6}$

text: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of 18 km/h. A boat, moving with speed of 36 km/h in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are $______$ and $______$ respectively.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The speed of river is $v_{r}=18\times \frac{5}{18}=5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

The speed of boat in still water is $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{b}}=36\times \frac{5}{18}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

The width of river is $\mathrm{w}=200\mathrm{m}$


[IMG]


The time taken to cross a river is determined solely by the component of the boat's velocity perpendicular to the river banks.

$t=\frac{w}{v_{b}\sin θ}$

Where theta is the angle with the bank. Time is minimum when the boat heads straight across ( $θ=90^{\circ }$ ), so $\sin θ=1$.

$t_{\min 1\to 2}=\frac{w}{v_{b}}=\frac{200}{10}=20\mathrm{s}$

Also, while returning to initial bank in minimum time,

$t_{\min 2\to 1}=\frac{w}{v_{b}}=\frac{200}{10}=20\mathrm{s}$

Total time of journey is,

$\mathrm{T}_{\text{total}}=\mathrm{t}_{\min 1\to 2}+\mathrm{t}_{\min 2\to 1}=2\times 20=40\mathrm{s}$

When the boat heads straight across to minimize time, the river flow carries it downstream. This horizontal distance is,

Drift (one way) $=\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{r}}\times \mathrm{t}_{\text{\min }1\to 2}=5\times 20\mathrm{s}=100\mathrm{m}$ east

The boat again heads straight across to minimize time. The river still flows from west to east, so the boat drifts another 100 m east.

Total Displacement along the bank:

$\Delta \mathrm{x}=100\mathrm{m}\text{(east)}+100\mathrm{m}\text{(east)}=200\mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the minimum time is 40 s and the displacement along the bank is 200 m . Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of M. Two blocks of mass of M and m are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is $________ ($assume no slipping of string on pulley).

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a hoop of mass $M$ and radius $R$, the moment of inertia is given as,

$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{rim}}=\mathrm{MR}^{2}$

Each rod has mass $M$ and length $L=2R$. The moment of inertia of a rod rotating about its center is $\frac{1}{12}ML^{2}$.

$\mathrm{I}_{\text{rod}}=2\times \frac{1}{12}\mathrm{M}(2\mathrm{R})^{2}=\frac{8\mathrm{MR}^{2}}{12}=\frac{2}{3}\mathrm{MR}^{2}$

Total moment of inertia of the system is,

$\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_{\text{rim}}+\mathrm{I}_{\text{rod}}=\mathrm{MR}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}\mathrm{MR}^{2}=\frac{5}{3}\mathrm{MR}^{2}$

Let a be the linear acceleration of the blocks and $α$ be the angular acceleration of the pulley. Assuming no slipping, $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{R}α$.


[IMG]


For Mass M,

$\mathrm{Mg}-\mathrm{T}_{1}=\mathrm{Ma}\ldots \text{(i)}$

For Mass m,

$\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{mg}=\mathrm{ma}.$

The net torque $τ$ about the centre of pulley is provided by the difference in tensions:

$τ=(\mathrm{T}_{1}-\mathrm{T}_{2})\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{I}α$

Substituting $\mathrm{I}=\frac{5}{3}\mathrm{MR}^{2}$ and $α=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{R}}$ :

$\begin{array}{ll} (\mathrm{T}_{1}-\mathrm{T}_{2})\mathrm{R} & =\left (\dfrac{5}{3}\mathrm{MR}^{2}\right )\dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{1}-\mathrm{T}_{2} & =\dfrac{5}{3}\mathrm{Ma}\ldots (\text{iii}) \end{array}$

Adding equations (i) and (ii):

$\begin{array}{l} (Mg-T_{1})+(T_{2}-mg)=Ma+ma \\  \\ \Rightarrow (M-m)g-(T_{1}-T_{2})=(M+m)a \end{array}$

Substituting the value of ( $\mathrm{T}_{1}-\mathrm{T}_{2}$ ) from equation (iii) :

$(M-m)g-\frac{5}{3}Ma=(M+m)a$

$\Rightarrow$ $(M-m)g=(M+m)a+\frac{5}{3}Ma$

$\Rightarrow$ $(M-m)g=\left (M+m+\frac{5}{3}M\right )a$

$\Rightarrow$ $(M-m)g=\left (\frac{8}{3}M+m\right )a$

$\Rightarrow$ $a=\frac{(M-m)g}{\left (\frac{8}{3}M+m\right )}$

Therefore, the acceleration of the blocks is $\frac{(M-m)g}{\left (\frac{8}{3}M+m\right )}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

The charge stored by the capacitor C in the given circuit in the steady state is $__________$ µC.

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 21st January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the steady state the capacitor branch carries no current, so the $2\Omega$ resistor has no voltage drop and the capacitor voltage equals the potential difference between the left and right junctions.

The longer plate of the cell is on the left, so the left junction is at the higher potential. Diode $D_{1}$ (in the $3\Omega$ branch) points from right to left, so it is reverse-biased and carries no current; diode $D_{2}$ (in the $4\Omega$ branch) points from left to right, so it is forward-biased and acts as a closed switch.


[IMG]

Only the loop of the cell, $1\Omega$ and $4\Omega$ carries current:

$i=\dfrac{2.5}{1+4}=0.5\text{A}$

The capacitor is in parallel with the $4\Omega$ resistor:

$V=4\times 0.5=2.0\text{V}$

$Q=CV=5μ\text{F}\times 2.0\text{V}=10μ\text{C}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
